newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders see LME nickel falling further.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME nickel falling further.

text.p: London Metal Exchange nickel prices are likely to slip further towards the next support at $7,100 due to technical factors following a dive of more than $200 on Tuesday, Asian traders said on Wednesday.
"I wouldn't be surprised if the price dropped further towards the next support seen at $7,100," said one trader.
"But it's dangerous to sell too aggressively amid talk of strikes at Inco."
At 0230 GMT, LME benchmark three-month nickel was quoted at $7,295/315 a tonne, little changed from $7,280/300 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday and the afternoon kerb close of $7,301.
The trader noted that Japanese players had placed buy orders at around $7,500 on Tuesday, a point that was overwhelmed by strong selling by speculators.
Copper was quoted at $2,508/13 a tonne, compared with $2,507/13 at 1800 GMT, and the kerb close of $2,507. Aluminium was $1,633/37, compared with $1,632/33 and $1,636 respectively.
On Tuesday in London, nickel spiralled lower on disappointment selling for liquidation and technical reasons, while aluminium drifted off its highs and copper consolidated at easier levels.
Asian traders said aluminium and copper could consolidate in the near future, fluctuating in a narrow range following strong gains earlier this month.
Zinc, however, was seen strong, with some traders expecting the metal to head towards $1,400 despite emerging selling by producers.
